::: {#sol-decimal-numeral}

Read from left to right, a numeral goes through four stages, and a string that is not a numeral can go wrong at any point.
Give the DFA one state for each thing it has to remember:

- $n_0$: nothing has been read yet;
- $n_1$: one or more $\mathtt{d}$s and nothing else, which is a numeral, so $n_1$ is accepting;
- $n_2$: one or more $\mathtt{d}$s and then a point, which is not a numeral yet;
- $n_3$: one or more $\mathtt{d}$s, a point and one or more $\mathtt{d}$s, which is a numeral, so $n_3$ is accepting;
- $n_4$: the string has already gone wrong, which is a dead state (@def-dead-state).

A $\mathtt{d}$ moves $n_0$ to $n_1$ and $n_2$ to $n_3$, and keeps $n_1$ at $n_1$ and $n_3$ at $n_3$.
A point moves $n_1$ to $n_2$.
A point anywhere else goes wrong: at the start, right after another point, or after the digits that follow a point.
@fig-numeral draws this DFA.
For example, its run (@def-run) on $\mathtt{dd.d}$ is $n_0, n_1, n_1, n_2, n_3$, which ends at an accepting state,
and its run on $\mathtt{d.}$ is $n_0, n_1, n_2$, which does not.

::: {#fig-numeral}
